content.comment_body: Hello all, I’m new to [product_name] and have completed a few projects using the basic module. I’m currently trying to connect an extension module to the PLC, but it’s not being detected after powering on—there’s no run/stop indication. Both modules share the same 24V supply. I attempted to connect PLC [article_no] with IO extension card [article_no], but faced the same issue. I also tried the PLC [article_no] with an analog card [article_no], and still had the same problem. I replaced both PLC and extension cards individually with new ones, but the issue persists. Since all the hardware is brand new, it seems unlikely all are faulty. Am I missing something? Do the cards need to be configured in the software? I haven’t found any configuration options for extension cards.

There’s no configuration required for extension modules in [product_name] programming software. The base module should automatically detect an expansion module as long as the module’s power supply is connected and the contact slide is properly engaged.

Thanks for the information. Upon checking, I discovered that someone had altered the polarity of the 24V supply on my test bench. Since the extension card is polarity sensitive, it wasn’t powering on. After correcting the polarity, the issue was resolved.
Glad to hear the problem has been solved.

analysis.insight_summary: The user had trouble getting the [product_name] base module to detect expansion modules, even after switching combinations of new hardware. The root cause was an incorrect power supply polarity, which wasn’t clearly indicated by the system. The lack of effective diagnostic feedback made troubleshooting difficult for new users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect expansion modules to be detected automatically and installation to be simple, with clear feedback if something goes wrong. They also look for possible configuration settings in the software for extension modules.
